scope: Corollary 8.3 (Cut, deletion, and clustering hardness) of the manuscript “The Unique Games Theorem” (preprints/The-Unique-Games-Theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 102 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 04d0290a9cb7ee81), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 42. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed real constant C > 1, it is NP-hard to approximate each of the four minimization problems above within factor C. For Sparsest Cut, this is hardness of the search task under polynomial-time Cook reductions: the algorithm must output a cutset, not only an estimate of the optimum. Consequently, unless P = NP, none of these problems admits a deterministic polynomial-time approximation with any fixed constant factor.
